item.title: edn_done 使用组合逻辑生成，未用寄存器同步

results.summary: edn_done is intentionally the local completion condition edn_req & edn_ack. The reviewed keymgr RTL shows a synchronous handshake path, not a bug caused by an unregistered pulse.
results.root_cause: The RTL defines edn_done as a local handshake completion in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv line 43 and uses it in clocked logic at lines 48-56 and 85-109.
results.reasoning: In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv, edn_req is a flop (lines 48-56), edn_ack is returned by the local EDN request wrapper instance (lines 63-78), and edn_done is simply their conjunction (line 43). That pulse clears edn_req (lines 51-52), enables the reseed counter after the first completed transaction (lines 85-90), clears the counter through prim_count (line 100), and is forwarded as reseed_done_o (line 61). The reviewed keymgr-local RTL does not show a combinational feedback loop or any consumer that treats edn_done as an asynchronous event. The formal property requiring $stable(edn_done) every cycle is itself inconsistent with the intended pulse semantics.
results.formal_alignment: Not aligned. A completion pulse is expected to toggle, so the reported FAIL on $stable(edn_done) does not indicate the claimed bug.

results.summary: There is no external edn_done input in this module. The signal is an internal local handshake-complete term and the report's 'externally controlled pulse' premise is incorrect.
results.root_cause: edn_done is declared locally and assigned internally in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv lines 37-43; reseed_done_o simply forwards it at line 61.
results.reasoning: The only EDN-facing inputs in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv are edn_i and the ack/data returned by prim_edn_req (lines 24-31 and 63-78). edn_done is not a port and cannot be externally driven. The module computes it internally as edn_req & edn_ack (line 43), then uses it to terminate the request (lines 51-52), report reseed completion (line 61), and clear the reseed counter (line 100). The claimed source-definition contradiction does not exist in the RTL.

item.title: adv_matrix[OwnerInt] data uses creator_seed, but adv_dvalid[OwnerInt] is owner_seed_vld

results.summary: The OwnerIntermediate advance path feeds creator_seed into KMAC but validates owner_seed instead. That is a real data/valid mismatch in the local RTL.
results.root_cause: In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv, adv_matrix[OwnerInt] is built from {sw_binding, creator_seed} at line 462, but adv_dvalid[OwnerInt] is driven from owner_seed_vld at line 463. This conflicts with the documented OwnerIntermediateKey inputs in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/doc/theory_of_operation.md lines 75-84.
results.trigger_condition: A software advance operation issued while keymgr_ctrl is in StCtrlCreatorRootKey. keymgr_ctrl selects stage_sel_o = OwnerInt on advance in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 581-588, and invalid_data[OpAdvance] then checks adv_dvalid[stage_sel] in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 555.
results.security_impact: If creator_seed is all-0 or all-1 but owner_seed looks valid, the CreatorRootKey -> OwnerIntermediateKey derivation can proceed with invalid creator diversification input and without the intended invalid-input rejection. Conversely, an invalid owner_seed can incorrectly block this transition even though owner_seed is not the data being hashed on this step.
results.reasoning: The documented data for reaching OwnerIntermediateKey is CreatorSecret + SoftwareBinding in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/doc/theory_of_operation.md lines 75-84. The RTL data path matches that: /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 462 uses creator_seed. However, the validity gate for that same stage is owner_seed_vld at line 463, and the debug latch for that stage also reports invalid_owner_seed when adv_en & (stage_sel == OwnerInt) at line 543. keymgr_ctrl selects OwnerInt as the target stage for advance from StCtrlCreatorRootKey in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 587-588, and the KMAC invalid-input check uses adv_dvalid[stage_sel] in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 555. This means the checked validity bit does not correspond to the actual data fed to KMAC on this transition.
additional_findings: The associated debug indication is also mismapped: /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 543 reports invalid_owner_seed for the OwnerInt transition even though the actual data path at line 462 uses creator_seed.

item.title: ctrl_rand and data_rand derive from opposite halves of the LFSR

results.summary: The RTL intentionally derives ctrl_rand and data_rand from different views of the same reseeded 64-bit LFSR state. That is a design choice, not a demonstrated local bug.
results.root_cause: The derivation is explicit in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 234-241, and the LFSR is reseeded from EDN through /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv lines 59-78.
results.reasoning: ctrl_rand[0:1] and data_rand[0:1] are assigned from opposite halves of the same lfsr plus a fixed permutation in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 237-241. The same LFSR is periodically reseeded from EDN via keymgr_reseed_ctrl (/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv lines 59-78). The reviewed keymgr-local spec does not require these two buses to be statistically independent streams, only that the PRNG be reseeded and used for control/data randomization. The finding raises a crypto-quality question, but it does not establish a concrete RTL defect in this module.

item.title: When init_q is high and en_i is high, init_q remains 1 regardless of init_i

results.summary: That behavior is exactly how keymgr_cfg_en is designed to work. init_q is a latched 'initialized' state, not a one-cycle sample register that must track init_i afterward.

item.title: vld_state_change_q may be asserted for longer than a single cycle

results.summary: A single qualifying state transition produces a one-cycle pulse. The RTL does not show one transition re-triggering state_change_err across multiple cycles.
results.root_cause: vld_state_change_d is defined as (state_d != state_q) and a tracked destination state in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 815-819, then flopped into vld_state_change_q at lines 822-827.

That value is flopped once into vld_state_change_q at lines 822-827 and consumed by state_change_err at line 833. On the next cycle after a completed transition, state_q has already moved to state_d, so the predicate state_d != state_q naturally drops unless there is a new distinct transition. The relevant transition sites at lines 555-557, 575-576, 595-596, and 615-616 are single-step state updates. So one transition yields one pulse; consecutive pulses would require consecutive real transitions, not one transition stretching across cycles.
results.formal_alignment: Not aligned. The manual RTL review did not find a mechanism for one state change to hold vld_state_change_q high for multiple cycles.
